subject: CarbonBridge - controlled deletion schedule and log evidence request
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@carbonbridge.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@carbonbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Controlled deletion and longer tenant log retention for regulated customers

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving quickly and have a request from our compliance group. One of our pilots must retain full request/response debug logs for 180 days rather than the platform default 30 days. At the same time, we need a defensible "proof of delete" process for when the retention window expires.

Can Redwood support a customer-scoped retention exception (tenant-scoped), with the following delivered artifacts?
- A written runbook describing the deletion workflow (how objects are identified, tombstoned, and purged)
- Signed manifests (file lists + hashes) at retention expiration
- Attestation that deleted objects are removed from primary storage and backups within X days
- If applicable, guidance on how logs will be segregated to limit blast radius

We're preparing a SIG/CAIQ and included preliminary questions (attached). Can you confirm feasibility, likely SLAs for evidence delivery, and any approvals you need internally?

Best,
Sasha

Attachments: carbonbridge_SIG_questions_20270726.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@carbonbridge.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled deletion and longer tenant log retention for regulated customers

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear ask and the SIG attachment. I'm confident we can support a tenant‑scoped retention extension for debug/audit logs, but there are tradeoffs we should align on. High level:

- Feasibility: Yes — we can provision per-tenant retention policies that extend TTLs to 180d for session/debug logs. To meet your proof-of-delete requirement we provide an evidence pack (manifest + checksums + deletion timestamps).
- Delivery SLA for evidence: Standard turnaround is 5 business days after retention expiry. For pilot customers we can offer expedited collection (48–72 hrs) under a paid addendum.
- Backups: We do not promise immutable backups indefinitely. We will document backup retention windows and the expected window for scrub from backups; for most configurations that is within 14 days of primary purge unless otherwise contractually agreed.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal approvals: I will loop in Naomi (compliance) and Marissa (ops) to assemble the deletion playbook and evidence template.
2) Draft a short addendum to the SOW that documents the retention extension and SLAs.
3) Create a delivery checklist for SOC2 auditor review.

I'll follow up with a proposed playbook and checklist by end of day tomorrow.

—Mateo

Subject: Re: Controlled deletion and longer tenant log retention for regulated customers

Thanks Mateo / Sasha — I reviewed the SIG questions and sketched what compliance will require to sign off. A few practical constraints and asks from our side: 

- Separation: To minimize scope for backups and forensic hold, we prefer to route the 180d logs to a tenant-scoped bucket/prefix with distinct lifecycle rules. That makes manifests and deletions auditable.
- Proof-of-delete artifacts: we require (a) content manifest (filename, size, SHA256), (b) deletion transaction id, (c) timestamp and operator id, (d) snapshot of object metadata prior to deletion. We can produce those as CSV + signed OTP.
- Backup purge window: For standard infra the backup window is 14 days; for a contractual change we need an exception in the contract to delay backup prune to align with retention. That requires Legal/Commercial approval.
- Legal hold trigger: If CarbonBridge invokes legal hold, we will stop automated deletion and provide a hold workflow. We need Legal contact to confirm escalation flow.

I'll assemble a draft playbook (redwood_proof_of_delete_playbook_v1.pdf) and a sample manifest CSV for your review. Marissa — can you confirm operational feasibility for exporting manifests at TTL expiration?

Naomi

Attachments: redwood_proof_of_delete_playbook_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sasha Ivanov <sasha@carbonbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled deletion and longer tenant log retention for regulated customers

Hi all — quick ops note on how we'd implement this without touching backups immediately: 

- Implementation approach: configure tenant-scoped ingest to a dedicated S3 prefix (tenant/carbonbridge/debug-logs/). Set lifecycle for 180d. At TTL expiry an automated job will generate a manifest (CSV) and a signed deletion event. The job will then perform object DELETEs and write a deletion record to our audit store.
- Manifests: we will create s3_manifest_carbonbridge_20270728.csv sample output with fields: key, size, sha256, lastModified, deletion_timestamp, deletion_tx_id. We'll include a human-friendly proof-of-delete summary PDF.
- Backups: default backup pruning will run 14 days after primary purge. If CarbonBridge needs backup exclusion we need an addendum and ~3 weeks lead time to update snapshot policies.
- Cost: extended retention increases storage + retrieval costs. I'll include an estimate in the addendum.

Sasha — if that matches your needs I can schedule a 30‑minute tech-runbook review with your infra team tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa
